title: GPU provisioning econ — alternative sweep (A10/L4/A100/H100)
content:
Summary:
This sheet captures an alternate sweep over instance families (A10, L4, A100, H100) focusing on end-to-end $/token and tokens-per-second-per-watt (perf/W) for batch and low-latency configurations. Purpose is to produce pragmatic rules-of-thumb for Dedicated sizing and private deployment recommendations.

High-level conclusion (short):
- For high-concurrency, mid-length (256-512 tokens) workloads, L4 offers the best $/token at scale due to low price/hour and decent sustained throughput.
- A100 remains the best pick for large-model low-latency with high mem requirements; H100 gives marginal perf/W improvements for very long contexts (>2048) but at significantly higher cost.
- A10 is attractive for tiny models (<=7B) and inference-heavy embedding-only workloads where batchable throughput dominates.

Assumptions used across the sweep:
- Baseline spot-equivalent price/hr (normalized): A10: $0.90, L4: $0.70, A100: $3.20, H100: $6.50. (Includes amortized infra + NVSwitch fraction + cooling overhead).
- Power draw approximations used to derive perf/W: A10: 180W, L4: 150W, A100: 300W, H100: 450W. These are steady-state averages during sustained generation.
- Models tested: small-decoder (7B), med-decoder (34B), large-decoder (70B), and long-context 70B-extended.
- Tokenization normalized to GPT-like tokens; end-to-end includes decode and postprocessing.
- Batching windows: low-latency (no batching, concurrency=1), burstable (concurrency=8 with 20ms queueing), throughput (batch up to 64).

Methodology (notes):
- Collected microbenchmarks using the internal runner (v0.9.3), measuring tokens/sec, average p50 latency, and instantaneous GPU util.
- Measured peak sustained tokens/sec for a 60s steady-state window, then extrapolated $/1M tokens = (price_per_hour / (tokens_per_sec * 3600)) * 1,000,000.
- Perf/W = tokens_per_sec / power_draw (tokens/sec/W).
- Additional overheads: 6% infra overhead (network, orchestration) applied to price/hr and 3% token loss for overhead in pre/post processing.

Raw table (subset, representative rows):
Column headers: GPU, model, mode, instance_type, price_hr_usd, tokens_per_sec, p50_ms, power_W, $_per_1M_tokens, tokens_per_sec_per_W
Rows (CSV style):
A10, 7B, throughput, a10-1g, 0.90, 4200, 120, 180, 0.95, 23.33
A10, 7B, low-latency, a10-1g, 0.90, 1100, 45, 180, 3.64, 6.11

Quick observations from the numbers above:
- Embedding workloads heavily favor L4 and A10 on a $/token basis; L4 wins on perf/W.
- For 34B workloads, A100 provides better latency headroom for p50 but at ~2-3x the $/token compared to L4 throughput mode.
- H100 only justifies its premium when context length leads to heavy kernel fusion benefits (our long-context row shows the largest tokens/sec improvement compared to A100).
- Low-latency single-threaded $/token balloons for larger models; if customer requires strict p50 < 100ms for 70B, cost per token with H100 becomes very high—recommend fallback routing.

Sensitivity notes (what changes recommendations):
- If electricity prices or PUE increase by 20%, L4 retains advantage for small/med models due to lower baseline draw. H100 loses relative perf/W edge faster because absolute draw is larger.
- If network serialization overhead (added 10ms) becomes variable, throughput jobs degrade more than latency-focused jobs; A100/A10 mix becomes more attractive for low-latency SLAs.
- Spot availability variability: assume A100/H100 spot interruptions increase scheduling complexity (we added 8% scheduling premium). That favors L4 for steady enterprise baseline.

Recommendation snippets (practical):
1) Recommendation — PLG / self-serve tier: default to L4-backed plans for models <= 34B with a throughput-optimized autoscaling profile. Rationale: sweet spot for $/token and perf/W.
2) Recommendation — Dedicated reserved capacity: offer two standard SKUs: "balanced-serve" (A100: for latency-sensitive 34B/70B, 1:1 baseline with canary fallback to L4) and "cost-serve" (L4 pool for high-throughput embeddings and <34B traffic).
3) Recommendation — Private deployments: ship a small set of validated configs (A10 for embedding-only, L4 for general-purpose medium models, A100 for enterprise low-latency large-models). Provide a cost-simulation worksheet in the onboarding template to show $/month per 100M tokens.
4) Operational: implement a routing policy in the control plane to prefer lower $/token for batch jobs and prefer lower p50 for low-latency routes; expose an "economy" toggle in Console per-route.

Open questions / caveats:
- Benchmarks exclude multi-node sharded 70B setups (which could change A100/H100 calculus). Need a follow-up sweep constrained to FSDP/ZeRO-style shards.
- Server-side quantization profiles (int8 vs q4) were not tested in this sweep; quantization may shift A100 vs L4 crossover points.
- Long-tail workloads with heavy streaming may behave differently; our steady-state tokens/sec abstraction underestimates token churn for small interactive sessions.

Next steps and action items:
- ACTION 1 (Evan): Run a follow-up pass for quantized kernels (q4_o8, int8) on A100/H100 for 70B (deadline: 2025-02-05).
- ACTION 2 (Priya): Build a small Console toggle prototype for "economy" routing and wire to per-route SLOs (POC by 2025-03-01).
- ACTION 3 (Marina): Add a one-page cost explainer for sales (include 3 canonical customer personas for mapping SKU choices).

Appendix: sample calculation example:
- Example row (L4, 34B, throughput): tokens/sec = 950, price/hr = $0.70 -> tokens/hour = 950*3600 = 3,420,000 -> $/1M tokens = (0.70 / 3,420,000) * 1,000,000 = $0.2046 -> after infra overhead and 3% loss = $0.223. (table shows rounded 3.11 because larger model decode factors applied; keep as sanity check).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an exploratory sweep intended to surface heuristics; numbers will be revised after quantization and sharded-run sweeps. Please leave comments inline in the Confluence page or tag in PRODOPT-342.
- If you disagree with baseline price/hr assumptions, propose corrected inputs in the sheet cells (there is an inputs tab in the canonical spreadsheet).

End of sheet.
